label: Queue message
description: A message on a queue, consumed while a startup step names @queue/worker.port.json#consume. The body is decoded as JSON into request.message (typed by settings.message); the message's headers, its id, the queue and how many times it has been delivered are in the context too, and the guarding plugin adds the caller it identified from a credential the trigger reads out of the headers. The trigger's input mapping picks what the graph gets; its policies decide before the graph runs. The answer is judged against out and recorded; nobody receives it. A refusal is acknowledged, retried or dead-lettered as settings.outcomes maps its reason; every reason the trigger can reach must be mapped (T005). A fault becomes settings.onFault, retry by default. A retry past maxAttempts is dead. A message whose input does not conform is dead at once, since delivering it again cannot help.

connection.description: a connection document whose kind declares delivery: the broker

queue.description: the queue's name on that broker

message.description: the edge type of the message body, request.message; a shape with no blob field at any depth (X404)

maxAttempts.description: deliveries before retry becomes dead, a whole number of 1 or more; default 5

backoffMs.description: the wait before the second delivery, doubled before each further one, a whole number of 0 or more; default 1000

onFault.description: what a fault -- a node that broke with no reason -- becomes; default retry

outcomes.description: reason -> ack | retry | dead: what each refusal the run can reach means to the message, e.g. { "missing": "ack", "upstream": "retry" }

id.description: the broker's id for this message

attempt.description: 1 on the first delivery, one more on each redelivery

queue.description: the queue the message arrived on

headers.description: what the publisher put beside the body; where a credential rides

message.description: the message body, of the type settings.message names
